Set up the project dictionary

Source: R/dict-tools.R
use_dictionary.Rd

Writes a starter dict.yml and the JSON Schema an editor checks it against. It says what it will write, then writes it: the call is the consent, and it never asks. suppressMessages() silences it.

Usage

use_dictionary(path = ".")

Arguments

path

A directory in the project.

Value

The paths written, relative to the root, invisibly (character() when nothing was written).

Details

It writes, under the project root (see below):

  • dict.yml, only when there is none: a starter that reads as a dictionary with no keys, with two examples commented out. An existing dict.yml is never changed; when it has no yaml-language-server schema line, or one that points somewhere else than _weft/dict.schema.json, use_dictionary() prints the line to use.

  • _weft/dict.schema.json, when it is missing or differs from the schema of this version of weft (it is weft's own file). The folder _weft/ is created if needed.

The project root is the nearest folder from path upward that holds _weft.yml, else _quarto.yml, else path itself; when it is not path, use_dictionary() says so and writes there.

Nothing is written through a symbolic link (dict.yml, _weft or the schema file being one is an error, before anything is written), and a failed write is a weft_tool_error naming the file: Wrote: names only files that were written.

The schema covers what an editor can see of a dictionary file; read_dict() checks more (see dict_file), and a file the schema accepts can still be refused when it is read.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
use_dictionary()
} # }
